newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Rural Press behind early in 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Rural Press behind early in 2nd half.

text.p: Newspaper and radio group Rural Press Ltd said on Thursday that trading for the first five weeks of the second half of the 1996/97 year had been slightly below last year.
Rural Press said that its history of profit growth would continue as long as economy improved.

"Trading for the first five weeks of the second half of the current financial year had been slightly below last year, indicative of the continuing difficult economy," Rural Press said when releasing its results for the half to December 31.
"Providing the economy improves, it was anticipated that the company's history of profit growth would continue," Rural Press said.
Earlier, Rural Press reported a four percent rise in first half net profit to A$16.96 million and set an unchanged four cent per share dividend.
Rural Press chairman John B. Fairfax said the results were satisfactory given the difficult conditions in regional and rural markets across Australia.
Sales growth of 15 percent for the half to A$156 million had been helped by acquisitions, with revenues from traditional areas at last year's levels.
"Advertising volumes in the agricultural newspapers and magazines were the same as last year, while regional newspaper volumes were slightly lower than last year," Rural Press said.
"Regional newspapers continued to be affected by the sluggish economy, particularly with retailing and real estate advertising," it said.
"The agricultural publications continued to be impacted by the ongoing difficulties in the beef and wool sectors."
Offshore earnings gains in the U.S. publications were offset by lower returns from New Zealand.
Rural Press' share price closed unchanged at A$4.10, despite the market's one percent rise overall to a record high.
